Only one thread can execute any static synchronized method of the same class at a time.</li><li>Synchronized instance methods use the <b>object lock</b> (<i>account</i>). Only one thread can execute any synchronized instance method on the same object at a time.</li><li>Non-synchronized static methods can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously (<b>no class lock</b>).</li><li>Non-synchronized instance methods can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously (<b>no object lock</b>).</li><li>Static synchronized methods and instance synchronized methods do not block each other because they use different locks (<b>class lock vs object lock</b>).</li></ul>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="160" width="1126.23" x="-13.12" y="1140" as="geometry" /> ul.li: Synchronized static methods use the class lock (BankAccount.class). Only one thread can execute any static synchronized method of the same class at a time.
Synchronized instance methods use the object lock (account). Only one thread can execute any synchronized instance method on the same object at a time.
Non-synchronized static methods can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously (no class lock).
Non-synchronized instance methods can be executed by multiple threads simultaneously (no object lock).
Static synchronized methods and instance synchronized methods do not block each other because they use different locks (class lock vs object lock).
